issues.legal_issue: A person in admitted possession cannot be dispossessed in execution of a decree that does not bind that person or order their eviction without due process of law.
material_facts: The appellant had been placed in possession of the premises by the tenant company, and his possession was admitted.
The purchaser knew of the appellant’s possession, but did not make him a party to the specific-performance suit or obtain a decree for his eviction in a proceeding against him.
The appellant was dispossessed in connection with execution of the decree while his application seeking adjudication of his right to remain in possession was pending.
There was no decree or order for eviction of the appellant.
issues.conclusion: The appellant was unlawfully dispossessed and had to be restored to possession pending adjudication of his application under Order 21, Rules 98 and 99 of the Code of Civil Procedure.
issues.legal_principle: A person in possession cannot be removed without due process of law. The executing court must adjudicate a claim to possession under Order 21, Rules 98 and 99 of the Code of Civil Procedure; the Court did not decide at this stage what rights arose from the appellant’s arrangement with his employer.

rule.if: execution_of_decree and admitted_possession and not eviction_decree_against_occupant and dispossessed_without_due_process and possession_claim_pending

predicates.execution_of_decree: The dispute arises from an attempt to obtain possession through execution of a court decree.
predicates.admitted_possession: The person’s possession of the property is admitted.
predicates.eviction_decree_against_occupant: A decree or order directs the eviction of that person from the property.
predicates.dispossessed_without_due_process: The person was removed from possession without a lawful process determining the right to remove them.
predicates.possession_claim_pending: The person has an unresolved application seeking adjudication of their right to remain in possession.

issues.definition: When a person in admitted possession is removed during decree execution without an eviction decree against them and has a pending claim to possession, that person must be restored pending adjudication.

issues.legal_issue: When an application to rescind a specific-performance contract and an application to adjudicate a possession claim are both pending in execution proceedings, the rescission application must be decided first.
material_facts: The heirs of the landlady had filed an application under Section 28 of the Specific Relief Act, 1963, seeking rescission of the contract.
The appellant’s application under Order 21, Rules 98 and 99 of the Code of Civil Procedure, concerning his possession, was also pending.
issues.conclusion: The executing court was directed to decide the Section 28 application first and then dispose of the application under Order 21, Rules 98 and 99.
issues.legal_principle: In the circumstances of this case, the Court directed that the application under Section 28 of the Specific Relief Act, 1963, be decided before the pending application under Order 21, Rules 98 and 99 of the Code of Civil Procedure. No earlier cases were relied on for this direction.

predicates.execution_proceeding: The applications arise in proceedings to execute a court decree.
predicates.rescission_application_pending: A party has filed an unresolved application seeking rescission of a contract on which the decree is based.
predicates.possession_adjudication_application_pend: An unresolved application seeks adjudication of a person’s claim to possession in the execution proceedings.

issues.definition: If both a contract-rescission application and a possession-adjudication application are pending in execution proceedings, the rescission application is decided first.
